facts.text: Montello hosts Wisconsin’s largest cottonwood, the Montello Cottonwood, standing 138 feet tall with a 23.2‑foot trunk on Underwood Avenue near the courthouse.
The city was founded in 1849 when Josiah H. Dartt filed the first land claim in February that year.
In 1882 the Wisconsin Central Railroad built a spur to Montello, making it the eastern terminus that served the granite quarry.
The Montello Granite Company quarry operated until the 1970s, and its former site is now a park with waterfalls.
A woolen mill built by the Wisconsin Industrial Association in 1867 became one of the West’s most complete manufactories by 1876, processing 75,000 pounds of wool annually.
Montello’s name derives from a novel reference meaning “mountain” or “hill and water,” a meaning that inspired the founder’s house name.
